sections.html:
Bellevue is a high-value market. Median value for an owner-occupied home was $1,340,300 over 2020 to 2024, and 154,193 people live here as of July 1, 2025. Owners occupy about 52.0% of housing, median household income is $165,576 and median gross rent is $2,572. The city grew from 122,363 people in 2010 to 151,854 in 2020.

It is an Eastside city in King County, across Lake Washington from Seattle and between that lake and Lake Sammamish. Interstate 405 runs north to south, Interstate 90 crosses the southern part, and State Route 520 roughly marks the northern edge. Kirkland and Redmond sit to the north, Issaquah to the east, Mercer Island across the East Channel Bridge, and Newcastle and Renton to the south.

The city names fourteen neighborhoods:

  • Downtown, Wilburton/BelRed and Eastgate/Factoria.
  • Bridle Trails, Northwest Bellevue, Northeast Bellevue and West Bellevue.
  • Crossroads, Lake Hills, Newport and Somerset.
  • Cougar Mountain/Lakemont, Woodridge and West Lake Sammamish.

The great majority of the city is in the Bellevue School District, whose main public high schools are Bellevue High, Interlake, Newport and Sammamish. Parts of the city fall in the Lake Washington, Renton and Issaquah districts instead. Look up your address before listing, because buyers will ask.

Downtown Bellevue is the second largest city center in Washington, with about 1,300 businesses, 45,000 employees and 10,200 residents, and transit has caught up with the jobs. Sound Transit's 2 Line runs from Lynnwood to Redmond through Seattle, Mercer Island and Bellevue. The South Bellevue to Redmond Technology station section opened April 27, 2024, and the Seattle to Bellevue section opened in March 2026. The Bellevue Transit Center downtown serves both King County Metro and Sound Transit buses, and a fare-free electric shuttle run by Circuit began operating in August 2023.

Homes near a station can mention the walk to the train in the listing. Commute time across the city averages 23.6 minutes.

A whole house usually cannot be rented short term. Bellevue's Land Use Code defines transient lodging as a stay of less than 30 days, and an entire single-family home or a home with an accessory dwelling unit cannot be used that way. Rentals of 30 days or more are allowed, and an ADU may be rented only long term. If a buyer is counting on vacation-rental income, say so plainly in your listing.

Type of homeShort-term rental rule
Entire single-family home, or home with an ADUNot allowed for transient lodging.
Rooms in an owner-occupied single-family homeAllowed as a boarding house or bed and breakfast: owner-occupied, at most two rooms and two adults per room, with an approved home occupation permit (LUC 20.20.140).
Apartment, condo or planned unit development in a residential districtAllowed with a Short-Term Stay Use Registration Notice, limited to five units and 20% of the units in the development (LUC 20.20.800).

Development Services Land Use takes questions at 425-452-4188 or landusereview@bellevuewa.gov.

Bellevue Development Services publishes a list of work that requires permits. These are the items most likely to surface before a sale:

  • Additions that add square footage, including a second story or dormers, need a permit with plan review.
  • Converting a garage or carport into living space needs a permit with plan review.
  • Decks with a walking surface more than 30 inches above the ground need a permit with plan review.
  • Interior remodels that create new walls or turn a basement into living area need a permit.
  • Furnaces, heat pumps, new gas lines, new electrical circuits and EV charging stations need permits.
  • An interior accessory dwelling unit needs approval, and the review takes several weeks.

Some jobs need nothing. Replacing kitchen cabinets or countertops, swapping a window or door for the same size in the same spot, and building a fence under eight feet tall are all permit-free, though fences over 4.5 feet often cannot sit in front-yard setbacks. In an emergency, such as a failed water heater or furnace, repairs can start first and the permit follows on the first city work day afterward.

King County bills property tax on a Bellevue house, in two installments due April 30 and October 31 (RCW 84.56.020). The lien starts January 1. With no contract term on the subject, RCW 84.60.020 charges you for the days you owned the home that year and the buyer for the rest. Escrow prorates the bill at closing, and any unpaid balance comes out of your proceeds.

RCW 64.06.020 also requires a seller disclosure statement for improved residential property. The clock is five business days from mutual acceptance of the written contract, and the buyer can waive the form. A buyer who receives it can rescind within three business days.

On most sales the seller covers the state excise tax and escrow sends it to the county treasurer at closing. The state schedule for 2027 sales has four bands: 1.1% to $551,000, 1.28% to $1,551,000, 2.75% to $3,051,000, and 3% beyond that. At Bellevue's median home value of $1,340,300 a sale reaches the second band. A local portion is added, and your closing agent can give you the full figure before you sign.

Permit history draws the most questions in Bellevue. Collect records for any second story, dormer, garage or carport conversion, deck over 30 inches, basement remodel, furnace or heat pump, gas line, new circuit or EV charger. If an accessory dwelling unit exists, know whether it was approved and whether it is rented long term. Call Development Services if a record is missing, and expect that an interior ADU review takes several weeks. Having answers ready keeps a cash offer from stalling over a permit question.

sections.h2: What a sale looks like step by step
sections.html: First, check the school district and gather permit records for any addition, garage conversion, deck or remodel. Second, complete the disclosure statement. Third, ask your lender for a payoff figure and King County for the current tax balance. Fourth, once you accept an offer, escrow opens title work and prorates taxes. Fifth, you sign and the sale funds on closing day, with excise tax paid from your proceeds. With a cash buyer there is no bank appraisal or loan approval in the way, so the pace is set by title work and how quickly your papers are in order.

faqs.q: Can I rent my whole Bellevue house short term?
faqs.a: No. Bellevue does not allow an entire single-family home or a home with an ADU to be used for transient lodging, which is a stay under 30 days. Rentals of 30 days or more are allowed.

faqs.q: Does replacing kitchen cabinets in Bellevue need a permit?
faqs.a: A building permit is not required for replacing kitchen cabinets or countertops. A plumbing or electrical permit may still be needed if that work is part of the job.

faqs.q: Which school district serves my Bellevue home?
faqs.a: Most of the city is in the Bellevue School District, but portions are in the Lake Washington, Renton and Issaquah districts. Check the district for your exact address.

faqs.q: How soon must a Bellevue seller give the buyer the disclosure statement?
faqs.a: Five business days after both sides accept the written contract. The buyer can waive it, and some transfers are exempt. Once delivered, the buyer has three business days to rescind.

faqs.q: Who pays the state excise tax on a Bellevue sale?
faqs.a: Usually the seller, paid through escrow on the sale date. A local portion is added, so ask your closing agent for the total.
